lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Education appears before the more persuasive Experience and Projects sections.
items.because: More than three years of relevant engineering work carries the professional story better than the degree.

items.says: The résumé leaves 10 months between graduation and the first listed role unexplained.
“Improved update speed by 60%” does not define the measured quantity or its comparison point.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which part of the update improved or what baseline was used.

items.says: The test-rig bullet reports coverage and frequency but not what the testing accomplished.
items.because: It shows activity at scale without establishing the rig’s engineering value.

items.says: “Which found the root cause” makes the logger sound as though it performed the diagnosis itself.
An 8 kHz sampling rate cannot capture a 5 kHz signal without aliasing.
items.because: Its Nyquist frequency is 4 kHz, so the 5 kHz component will alias unless removed before sampling.

items.says: “Could capture it without aliasing” states an intended capability rather than an observed detector or validation result.
items.because: The practical effect of the signal-processing work remains unproven.

items.says: Declaring a shared counter volatile does not fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make access atomic or provide synchronization.

items.says: The race-condition claim does not identify the faulty behavior prevented or corrected.
items.because: Without that consequence, the importance of the fix remains unclear.

items.says: “On the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop” is unnecessarily wordy.
The same 300-robot firmware achievement is attributed to incompatible roles and date ranges.
items.because: It also appears in the Formula Student project, calling the accomplishment’s ownership and credibility into question.

items.says: “Rewrote the motor-controller firmware” does not show which technical decision produced the results.
items.because: The generic implementation does not connect the lower jitter and fault rate to a specific engineering change.

items.says: The strongest outcomes are buried after the implementation and fleet scope.
items.because: The line initially reads like a broad responsibility rather than a high-impact result.

items.says: The strongest Voltline bullet is not first in the entry.
items.because: Placing it last makes its production scope and before-and-after results less likely to be noticed.

items.says: “Automated end-of-line tests” does not identify the software, instrumentation, or test sequence automated.
items.because: A hardware-test hiring manager cannot see the specific automation skill behind the timing improvement.

items.says: The failure diagnosis does not explain how the solder-paste change was isolated as the cause.
items.because: Without a diagnostic method, the conclusion may read as correlation rather than systematic investigation.

items.says: “The findings updated the reflow profile” makes the findings perform the update.
items.because: Findings can prompt a process change but cannot implement one.

items.says: “The calibration procedure” does not identify the approach or technical change that addressed drift.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether this was sensor-calibration engineering or documentation of an existing process.

items.says: “Next-generation, innovation-driven” is generic promotional filler.
items.because: It offers no technical evidence and delays a concrete project description.

items.says: “IoT solution” is too vague to show how the station senses, processes, stores, or transmits data.
items.because: The label does not demonstrate embedded-systems skill beyond the project heading.

items.says: “Redefines sustainable environmental sensing” is unsupported hype that does not specify what changed or who benefited.
items.because: It is not tied to an observed result or baseline.

items.says: The quantified current-reduction bullet should open the project.
“Openly” is redundant after “Published.”
“Robot fleet’s motor controllers” is attributed to the wrong project.
items.because: Formula Student concerns a race car, while the résumé places robot-fleet work under Voltline Robotics.

items.says: The broad motor-controller line substantially duplicates the later robot-fleet rewrite.
items.because: It adds no distinct accomplishment and consumes space for Formula Student experience.

items.says: “Worked on firmware and testing” uses duty framing without identifying the firmware behavior or test.
items.because: It shows general participation rather than individual technical ownership.

items.says: The line does not say what changed because of the work.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it corrected a defect, enabled a function, or improved race readiness.

items.says: “CAN-bus” is incorrectly hyphenated.
items.because: The standard term is “CAN bus.”

items.says: The dashboard line does not identify the CAN function implemented or integration test performed.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the depth of the firmware work or reconstruct the integration approach.

items.says: “Before each race” gives the testing cadence but not what testing proved or improved.
items.because: Repeated testing does not establish that the firmware met requirements, caught faults, or operated reliably.

items.says: “Written and tested ... before each race” implies both activities were repeated before every race.
items.because: The firmware may have been written once while only validation recurred.

items.says: “Was written and tested” uses passive voice that hides the candidate’s ownership.
The CAN dashboard bullet should be first in the Formula Student entry.
The 300-robot firmware claim is attributed to the wrong project.
items.because: A Formula Student electric-car project is not a robot fleet, and the same accomplishment appears under Voltline Robotics.

items.says: “Rewrote motor-control firmware” does not identify the technical change that produced the result.
items.because: It omits the embedded technique behind the claimed improvement.

items.says: The jitter and motor-fault improvements do not define how either result was measured.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what jitter statistic, observation period, or fault definition produced them.

items.says: “FPGA” is listed without supporting experience, project, or education evidence.
items.because: A recruiter cannot tell where or how it was used and may treat it as keyword padding.
